worktrees.name: Worktrees
worktrees.process_running: A program started from this worktree is running ({{.Process}}), for example a dev server or a Gradle daemon. Stop it first.
worktrees.no_roots: No project folders to look in. Add the folders where you keep your code in Settings › Project folders.
worktrees.artifacts.title: Dependencies and builds in worktrees
worktrees.artifacts.what: node_modules, Pods, build and similar folders inside extra git worktrees, for example the ones Claude Code sessions create in .claude/worktrees.
worktrees.artifacts.why: Only folders that git ignores are listed, so your code and commits are not touched. Folders used by a running process (a dev server started from that worktree) can't be selected.
worktrees.artifacts.after: Before working in that worktree again, run npm install, pod install or a build to recreate them.
worktrees.builds.title: Leftover builds
worktrees.builds.what: Finished app builds lying next to the code: .xcarchive, .ipa, .apk, .aab, .dmg, .app and installers that git does not track.
worktrees.builds.why: They are build results, not source code, and can be built again from the project.
worktrees.builds.after: For an .xcarchive of a version that is live in the App Store, crash reports can no longer be symbolicated on this Mac — keep those.
